title: Proper refinement comparisons preserve the canonical forget-supports map
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $h:T\to B$ a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of arbitrary schemes [def-pc-scheme], and work in $D(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ for every scheme $V$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $F_a=La^*$ and $R_a=Ra_*$ with the canonical adjunctions of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], and $\kappa_{b,a}:R_bR_a\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{ba}$ for the canonical direct-image compositor [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], clause (5). A compactification $c=(j_c:T\hookrightarrow Z_c,r_c:Z_c\to B)$ means that $j_c$ is a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], $r_c$ is proper, and $r_cj_c=h$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. Put $J_c=D(j_{c!})$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], with open-adjunction unit $u_c:1\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{j_c}J_c$ as in [lem-asd-open-base-change-unit-mate]. Define $t_c:J_c\to R_{j_c}$ to be the $F_{j_c}\dashv R_{j_c}$ adjunct of $u_c^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], and define
$$\gamma_c=R_{r_c}(t_c);\kappa_{r_c,j_c}:R_{r_c}J_c\xrightarrow{\sim}R_h.$$
This is the proper forget-supports isomorphism [def-sp-unbounded-proper-shriek-star-comparison] computed with $c$.

Let $d=(j_d,r_d)$ be a second compactification and let $q:Z_c\to Z_d$ be a proper map with $qj_c=j_d$ and $r_dq=r_c$, such that the square $(1_T,j_c,j_d,q)$ is Cartesian. Let $b_q:F_qJ_d\xrightarrow{\sim}J_c$ be the inverse of the termwise open-extension base-change isomorphism of [lem-asd-open-base-change-unit-mate] for this square. With $\eta_q$ the unit of $F_q\dashv R_q$, define the specified refinement comparison
$$\rho_q=R_{r_d}(\eta_q J_d);R_{r_d}R_q(b_q);(\kappa_{r_d,q}J_c):R_{r_d}J_d\longrightarrow R_{r_c}J_c.$$
Then, as derived natural transformations in application order,
$$\rho_q;\gamma_c=\gamma_d.$$
In particular $\rho_q$ is invertible. For compactifications $c,d$ and a common refinement $e$ with proper maps $q_c:Z_e\to Z_c$ and $q_d:Z_e\to Z_d$ whose squares over $T$ are Cartesian, let $I_{c,d}=\rho_{q_c};\rho_{q_d}^{-1}:R_{r_c}J_c\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{r_d}J_d$. Then
$$I_{c,d};\gamma_d=\gamma_c.$$
This applies in particular to the canonical common refinement $\operatorname{inf}(c,d)$ used by rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationIso, hence to the actual comparison with a chosen compactification. There is no boundedness, Noetherian, nonempty-base, or finite-type-base assumption.

proof.text: First fix the normalization of composition, not just an isomorphism of endpoints. The categories of constant-$A$ module sheaves are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian]; every inverse image is exact additive with the specified direct-image right adjoint by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. The sheaf pullback compositor is conjugate to sheaf direct-image composition by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear]. Apply [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] to these exact functors and their specified adjoints. It identifies the resolution-defined derived compositor with the conjugate of the descended pullback compositor. Thus the $\kappa$ of clause (5) of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], in our inverse orientation, identifies the single-map adjunction with the composite adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. In particular, under $a_{b,a}:F_{ba}\simeq F_aF_b$ its counit is $F_a(\varepsilon_b R_a);\varepsilon_a$. The descended pullback compositor is the one used in [lem-kun-derived-pullback-composition-monoidal], whose associativity clause removes parenthesization ambiguity. All hypotheses here concern ordinary unbounded constant-ring categories on arbitrary schemes.

proof.text:
For $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ put $X=J_dK$ and $C=a_{q,j_c}:F_{j_d}\simeq F_{j_c}F_q$. In [lem-asd-open-base-change-unit-mate] take $j=j_d$, $a=q$, $j'=j_c$, $u=1_T$. Its $B_K:J_cK\simeq F_qJ_dK$ is $b_{q,K}^{-1}$, and its square comparison $c_X$ is $C_X$ after the canonical identity identifications. In application order its equation is
$$u_{c,K};F_{j_c}(B_K)=u_{d,K};C_X.$$
Postcompose by $F_{j_c}(b_{q,K});u_{c,K}^{-1}$ and precompose by $u_{d,K}^{-1}$. The inverse pairs cancel, giving
$$C_X;F_{j_c}(b_{q,K});u_{c,K}^{-1}=u_{d,K}^{-1}.$$
This uses exactly the supplied Cartesian square, and does not assert any base-change theorem for a non-Cartesian refinement.

source.place: First triangle, open-unit normalization; Stacks Tag 03S6, etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-shriek-base-change, with the explicit derived unit equation of the cited node.

proof.text:
Write $z=b_{q,K};t_{c,K}:F_qX\to R_{j_c}K$, $v=\eta_{q,X};R_q(z):X\to R_qR_{j_c}K$, and $s=v;\kappa_{q,j_c,K}:X\to R_{j_d}K$. By the normalization in step 1 and the composite Hom bijection of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], the transpose of $s$ under $F_{j_d}\dashv R_{j_d}$ is
$$C_X;F_{j_c}\bigl(F_q(v);\varepsilon_{q,R_{j_c}K}\bigr);\varepsilon_{j_c,K}.$$
The inner factor is $z$: expand $v$, move $F_qR_q(z)$ through $\varepsilon_q$ by its naturality, and cancel $F_q(\eta_{q,X});\varepsilon_{q,F_qX}=1$. Hence this transpose equals
$$C_X;F_{j_c}(b_{q,K});F_{j_c}(t_{c,K});\varepsilon_{j_c,K}
=C_X;F_{j_c}(b_{q,K});u_{c,K}^{-1}=u_{d,K}^{-1}.$$
The first equality is the definition of $t_c$ as the adjunct of $u_c^{-1}$; the second is step 2. By the bijective transpose correspondence [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], this is also the transpose of $t_{d,K}$, so $s=t_{d,K}$. The formulas are natural in $K$, giving an equality of derived natural transformations.

proof.text:
The maps $\gamma_c,\gamma_d$ are the canonical proper isomorphisms specified in [def-sp-unbounded-proper-shriek-star-comparison], with the displayed compactification formulas. Step 4 gives $\rho_q=\gamma_d;\gamma_c^{-1}$, so $\rho_q$ is invertible. Apply step 4 to the two supplied Cartesian proper refinements from $e$. It gives $\rho_{q_c};\gamma_e=\gamma_c$ and $\rho_{q_d};\gamma_e=\gamma_d$. The second equation implies $\rho_{q_d}^{-1};\gamma_d=\gamma_e$, and hence
$$I_{c,d};\gamma_d=\rho_{q_c};\rho_{q_d}^{-1};\gamma_d=\rho_{q_c};\gamma_e=\gamma_c.$$
Only inverses of the specified proper comparisons are used.

proof.text: Finally identify the particular comparison mentioned in the statement. Properness makes $h$ separated and of finite type, in particular quasi-compact, and $c$ supplies an open-then-proper factorization. Thus the last clause of [lem-pur-etale-graph-comparison-base-change] applies: on quasi-compact maps its comparison equals $\rho_{q_c};\rho_{q_d}^{-1}$, and is explicitly the source-library rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationIso. The definition in LowerShriekIndependenceUnbounded.lean uses precisely the two maps from $\operatorname{inf}(c,d)$, in this order. Step 5 therefore proves the stated equation for this actual comparison, including when $d$ is the chosen compactification. This is an application to the specified comparison, not a replacement by an arbitrary isomorphism. No argument imposed boundedness, Noetherianity, a nonempty base, or a finite-type base.

lemma rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationComparison_app_comp_toLowerStar
    (M : DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology A)) :
    (rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationComparison A r hcart).app M ≫
        R((c.g)_*[A]).map ((derivedOpenImmersionLowerShriekToLowerStar A c.i).app M) ≫
        (rightDerivedLowerStarCompHom A c.i c.g f c.comm).app M =
      R((d.g)_*[A]).map ((derivedOpenImmersionLowerShriekToLowerStar A d.i).app M) ≫
        (rightDerivedLowerStarCompHom A d.i d.g f d.comm).app M
lean.note: Existing upstream declarations, specialized to A = ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ for a finite commutative ring Λ and to proper f. The primary theorem is exactly ρ_q;γ_c=γ_d, componentwise for every derived object; NatTrans.ext gives the natural-transformation formulation. Its implicit binders are the coefficient category, arbitrary schemes X,Y, f, compactifications c,d, a refinement r, and its Cartesian square hcart. The second listed declaration supplies invertibility. Applying the primary theorem to e→c and e→d and cancelling the second comparison gives the arbitrary-common-refinement equation. The third listed theorem supplies the actual inf comparison equation directly; rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationIso is definitionally the infFst comparison followed by the inverse infSnd comparison. The fourth and fifth declarations fix exactly the unit/base-change/compositor and adjunct normalizations in the node; rightDerivedLowerShriekIsoRightDerivedLowerStar is its proper forget-supports isomorphism. All signatures and definitions were read in the live source; scompile.py --source confirmed the main module. No new module, helper or statement correction.
